Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself to handle smaller, simpler versions of that same problem. Think of it like Russian nesting dolls, where you keep opening the next smaller doll until you finally reach the tiny one in the very center. As each of these nested function calls finishes, it passes its result back up the chain until the original problem is completely solved.
